title: Florida State University Secures $2.1M Federal Grant for Campus-Scale Quantum Communication Testbed - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Florida State University received $2.1M in NIST Community Project Funding to build the southeastern U.S.'s first campus-scale quantum communication testbed linking a hub to receiver nodes at the FAMU-FSU College of Engineering and the National MagLab, stress-testing QKD under turbulence, 45+ Tesla fields and cryogenic cycling.

insights.claim: FSU won $2.1 million in federal Community Project Funding via NIST, supported by Rep. Daniel Webster, to build what is described as the first dedicated quantum communications testbed in the southeastern United States.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Earmark-style funding is spreading quantum infrastructure regionally, a modest demand source for networking hardware.
insights.locator: Florida State University (FSU) has been awarded

insights.claim: The testbed uses existing campus dark fiber and reconfigurable free-space optical channels to distribute entangled photon pairs between FSU's IRCB hub and two receiver nodes.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Reuse of dark fiber shows a low-cost path to quantum network trials.

insights.claim: Leveraging MagLab, the testbed will study how strong magnetic fields (up to 45+ Tesla) alter optical polarization via Faraday rotation and affect SNSPD performance.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Unique test regime could produce reliability data relevant to detector vendors.
insights.quote: investigating how strong magnetic fields alter optical polarization states (Faraday rotation)

insights.claim: The engineering-college link focuses on adaptive optics for free-space channel stabilization and full-stack protocol validation under atmospheric turbulence.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Free-space link robustness is a gating factor for practical QKD deployment.

insights.claim: The facility complements the 45-faculty FSU Quantum Initiative and the statewide Florida Alliance for Quantum Technology workforce pipeline.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Florida joins other states building quantum clusters.
